'''Tyler Bilodeau''' (born April 17, 2004) is an American [[basketball]] player for the [[Brooklyn Nets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Long Island Nets]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State Beavers]] and [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. He earned third-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] honors twice in the [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] with UCLA.

==Early life==
Bilodeau was born in [[Billings, Montana]],<ref name=ucla_profile>{{cite web|title=Tyler Bilodeau|publisher=UCLA Athletics|url=https://uclabruins.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/tyler-bilodeau/14479|access-date=March 14, 2025}}</ref> to 1991 [[National Hockey League]] first-round draft pick [[Brent Bilodeau]] and [[Women's National Basketball Association]] player [[Cass Bauer-Bilodeau]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pascoe |first1=Bruce |title=Seen and heard in Phoenix: Krivas' injury dims Wildcat hopes, plus familiar faces |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/arizona-mens-basketball-ucla-phoenix/article_03624486-ba56-11ef-aef1-83963096a565.html |website=Arizona Daily Star |access-date=March 17, 2025}}</ref> Tyler Bilodeau played both [[ice hockey|hockey]] and basketball growing up, before settling on basketball.<ref name=daschel_10112023/> As a [[senior (education)|senior]] at [[Kamiakin High School]] in [[Kennewick, Washington]], he averaged 22.7 points and 10.3 rebounds, while leading the team to a fourth-place finish in the Washington Class 4A state tournament. He was named Mid-Columbia Conference Player of the Year and honored as [[Washington Mr. Basketball]].<ref name=ucla_profile/><ref>{{cite news|first=Dave|last=Nichols|title=Prep notebook: Dylan Darling named boys 4A state player of the year; Jayden Stevens selected for all-tourney first team|date=March 9, 2022|newspaper=The Spokesman-Review|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2022/mar/09/prep-notebook-dylan-darling-named-boys-4a-state-pl/|access-date=May 8, 2025}}</ref>

Coming out of high school, Bilodeau was rated as a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to play [[college basketball|collegiately]] for the [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State Beavers]] over other schools such as [[Boise State Broncos men's basketball|Boise State]], [[Saint Louis Billikens men's basketball|Saint Louis]] and [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nemec |first1=Andrew |title=Tyler Bilodeau, 3-star forward, commits to Oregon State Beavers over Boise State, Washington State, others |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/recruiting/2021/10/tyler-bilodeau-3-star-forward-commits-to-oregon-state-beavers-over-boise-state-washington-state-others.html |website=OregonLive.com |date=October 28, 2021 |access-date=March 14, 2025}}</ref>

==College career==
=== Oregon State ===
As a [[freshman]] at [[Oregon State University]] in [[2022–23 Oregon State Beavers men's basketball team|2022–23]], Bilodeau made 13 [[starting lineup|starts]] and averaged 7.0 points and 3.9 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game.<ref name=daschel_10112023>{{cite web |last1=Daschel |first1=Nick |title=Oregon State forward Tyler Bilodeau changes number to honor his basketball star mother |date=October 11, 2023|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/2023/10/oregon-state-forward-tyler-bilodeau-changes-uniform-to-honor-his-basketball-star-mother.html |website=OregonLive.com |access-date=March 14, 2025}}</ref> On December 28, 2023, he recorded 10 points and 14 rebounds against [[2023–24 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Crosby |first1=Joseph |title=Oregon State forward Tyler Bilodeau announces transfer to UCLA men's basketball |url=https://dailybruin.com/2024/04/20/oregon-state-forward-tyler-bilodeau-announces-transfer-to-ucla-mens-basketball |website=The Daily Bruin |access-date=March 14, 2025}}</ref> In his [[sophomore]] year in [[2023–24 Oregon State Beavers men's basketball team|2023–24]], Bilodeau changed his jersey number from 10 to 34 in honor of his mother, who wore the number in college and professionally. "My mom is who I look up to. She's the reason I play basketball", he said.<ref name=daschel_10112023/> He averaged 14.3 points and 5.7 rebounds per game that season, while shooting 34.5% on his [[three-point field goal|three-pointers]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bolch |first1=Ben |title=UCLA adds major offensive firepower with addition of Oregon State's Tyler Bilodeau |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2024-04-20/ucla-basketball-adds-offensive-firepower-oregon-state-tyler-bilodeau |website=Los Angeles Times |date=April 20, 2024 |access-date=March 14, 2025}}</ref> His 53.3% [[field goal percentage]] ranked fourth in the [[Pac-12 Conference]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Bill|last=Seals|title=UCLA Men's Basketball announces the addition of two more to the Roster|date=May 9, 2024|newspaper=Culver City Observer|url=https://www.culvercityobserver.com/story/2024/05/09/sports/ucla-mens-basketball-announces-the-addition-of-two-more-to-the-roster/13640.html|access-date=March 14, 2024}}</ref> After the season, he entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]],<ref>{{cite web |last1=Daschel |first1=Nick |title=More hits to Oregon State men's basketball as forward Tyler Bilodeau heads to transfer portal |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/2024/04/more-hits-to-oregon-state-mens-basketball-as-forward-tyler-bilodeau-heads-to-transfer-portal.html |website=OregonLive.com |date=April 3, 2024 |access-date=March 14, 2025}}</ref> becoming one of the best shooting [[big man (basketball)|big men]] available.<ref>{{cite news|first1=Sam|last1=Vecenie|first2=CJ|last2=Moore|title=Ranking the best players in the NCAA men's basketball transfer portal|date=July 5, 2024|work=The Athletic|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5360188/2024/06/05/ncaa-transfers-portal-rankings-list/|url-access=subscription|access-date=March 14, 2025}}</ref>

victory |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2024-10-31/ucla-basketball-tyler-bilodeau-exhibition-win |website=Los Angeles Times |date=October 31, 2024 |access-date=March 14, 2025}}</ref> He played the entire [[2024–25 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2024–25 season]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|Bruins]] out of position at [[center (basketball)|center]], where he was the starter in each game that he played.<ref>{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=In a massive setback for UCLA, 7-3 center Aday Mara will not return next season|date=March 31, 2025|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2025-03-31/ucla-aday-mara-will-not-return|access-date=May 3, 2025}}</ref> On November 8, 2024, Bilodeau tallied 23 points and a career-high 15 rebounds in a loss to [[2024–25 New Mexico Lobos men's basketball team|New Mexico Lobos]].<ref name=ucla_profile/><ref>{{cite web |last1=Bolch |first1=Ben |title=Tyler Bilodeau's big game can't save UCLA in frustrating loss to New Mexico |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2024-11-08/ucla-loses-to-new-mexico-tyler-bilodeau |website=Los Angeles Times |date=November 9, 2024 |access-date=March 14, 2025}}</ref> On December 21, he tied his then-career-high with 26 points in a loss to [[2024–25 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]].<ref points per game, shooting a team-high 40.0  percent on 3-pointers, and ranked second on the Bruins in rebounding with 4.6 per game.<ref name=ucla_profile/> He was named third-team [[List of All-Big ==Professional career==
On June 24, 2026, Bilodeau was selected by the [[Brooklyn Nets]] with the 43rd overall pick in the [[2026 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |title=UCLA's Tyler Bilodeau Selected by Brooklyn in 2026 NBA Draft |url=https://uclabruins.com/news/2026/06/24/uclas-tyler-bilodeau-selected-by-brooklyn-in-2026-nba-draft |website=[[UCLA Bruins]] |access-date=July 5, 2026 |date=June 24, 2026}}</ref>
